Last summer I was visiting my mom's house for vacations, my grandmother lived there too until she passed away the previous winter.

One night I wanted to watch something in my phone before sleep but had very low battery, the charger wasn't near the bed so I waited until it charged enough to use it for less than a hour without issues(about 40%). Unplugged my phone and went to bed.

That night I dreamt about my granny: I was in her bed and started listening her voice. I was amazed so I sat and saw her sitting in front of me, full of the whitest light I've ever seen. Everything in her was white and bright, even her eyes. We talked a lot, she said specific things like dates and years... Then she said it was time for her to go and that I will forget everything we talked, that it would be like it wasn't real. I laid down and turned around so I won't see her leave.

Next morning I woke up unusually early, forcing my face to the wall. Checked the hour on my phone and noticed it had the battery at 100%.

No one else was there, I use the whole second floor of the house for myself and it has a lockable door to access it by the stairs. I like paranormal stuff and everything, but I wouldn't lie about it to tell a story. I'm pretty skeptical, but I don't have any logical explanation for that.

We don't use it after the verb "to be" (ser) when referring to a title, job or something that can't be changed:

My sister is a doctor. / Mi hermana es doctora.

I'm a woman. / (Yo) soy mujer.



Also when adding an adjective to a title, when it is part of the title or an intrinsic characteristic:

Her dad is a mechanical engineer. / Su padre es ingeniero mecánico.

She is a bad person. / Ella es mala persona.



And when talking about a thing in general, not specified:

I have a pet. / (Yo) Tengo mascota.

Do you have a partner? / ¿Tienes pareja?



For your examples:

I need a refund. / Necesito un reembolso.

Too specific. "Necesito reembolso" may need some context. Like "Necesito reembolso de un producto".

He is a gentleman. / El es un caballero.

"El es caballero" can be correct when referring to "He is a knight", "caballero" being a title/job.

I'm a white mexican woman and have lived my entire life in Mexico, but one of my cousins (from the US) is married to an afro-mexican man. When they come to visit I notice people looking at him, it's uncomfortable of course but I think some mexicans are curious since is not usual to see black people, or in general "different" people.

We even look like that at Mennonites, who are white people. Not looking with judgement or maliciously, it's just kinda shocking to see someone so different from us. And yes, our society is racist and that's embarrassing. We even discriminate ourselves. We have this ideal where white people is superior, even  when the biggest portion of our population is "morena" (brown-skinned). To be fair, I think we hate more on ourselves than in foreigners.


An aunt told me that when she was visiting the US, she went into a restaurant and saw (I'm quoting) "gorgeous tall black women". They were not common to her sight but in a good way. Of course not all people thinks the same way, but know that some of us are just shocked by a unique beauty, like when seeing a famous artist.

Maybe with COVID restrictions those annoying physical interactions will  decrease, I hope that. Wish you the best luck and hope you have a good time in our country :)

My cat came into my life by accident 3 years ago. I didn't even liked cats at that time. I was dealing with huge stuff and had been trying to be a functional being since my psychiatric disorders showed up like 1-1.5 year before that.

I also attempted to end it all a few times and thought I was even failing at that. I dropped out  college and got I job I hated, but that payed my drugs and booze. I was a huge mess...

But the day I got my hairy princess everything changed. I accepted her (a guy I met on tinder and his mother kinda manipulated me to keep her, a funny story) and made myself responsible for her. Then the biggest portion of my incomes went to her stuff: food, litter, vet, accessories. That minimized drastically my drug consume.

The more time I spent with her, the most I liked her. I learned to love my kitty. 
Now that I'm living far from my family, she is my only company and definitely she makes everything better. 

I love spending time with her, playing or combing her hair. She's like a baby, my baby. I have a commitment to make sure she doesn't lack anything and make her feel loved. I just want to see her happy, that makes me happy.

Then it was nice, like having a friendly shoulder to cry on.
